title: How to open a business bank account in the UAE
summary: Learn how to open a UAE business bank account, prepare the required documents, complete KYC, and compare account options for your company.
body_markdown:
Opening a business bank account in the UAE can be straightforward when your documents make sense. When they do not, the application can become a long correspondence about ownership charts and supplier invoices.


Banks and account providers need to understand who owns the company, where its money comes from, and how the account will be used. Preparing those answers early can reduce delays.

## What is a corporate bank account?


A corporate bank account is opened in a company’s legal name and used for its business transactions.


It can receive customer payments, pay suppliers and employees, and hold company funds. Depending on the provider, it may also support multiple currencies, corporate cards, payroll, international payments, and financing.


Keeping company money in a dedicated account also gives your accountant a cleaner record. They can review business activity without first asking why a supermarket payment is sitting between two supplier invoices.


## Why open a business bank account in the UAE?


A business bank account keeps your company’s money, payments and financial records organised.


### Keep company finances clear


A dedicated account separates company transactions from personal spending. This makes it easier to track revenue, expenses, outstanding payments, and cash available to the business.


### Receive and make business payments


Customers and suppliers generally expect payments to use an account bearing the company’s legal name. A dedicated account gives both sides a clearer transaction record.


### Support tax records


The[Federal Tax Authority](https://tax.gov.ae/en/taxes/corporate.tax.aspx) requires businesses to retain records that allow their tax position to be verified. Its[recordkeeping guidance](https://tax.gov.ae/en/media.centre/news/pr.28082025.aspx) states that relevant Corporate Tax records must generally be retained for at least seven years.


A separate account makes income and expenses easier to trace. It does not complete the tax return. Your accountant still has that pleasure.


### Control access to company money


Business accounts may support multiple users, approval permissions, and card controls. These features become useful once founders, finance staff, and department heads need different levels of access.


### Build a financial history


Regular account activity creates a financial record for the company. Banks may consider this history when assessing future applications for credit, trade finance, or other facilities.


## Eligibility and documents required


UAE mainland and free-zone companies can apply for business accounts. Approval depends on the provider’s eligibility rules and compliance review.


The[Central Bank of the UAE’s customer due diligence requirements](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/62-standard-customer-due-diligence) require financial institutions to identify customers and understand why an account is being opened.


Commonly requested documents include:


- A valid trade or professional license.
- Certificate of incorporation or registration.
- Memorandum and articles of association.
- Passport copies for shareholders, directors, and signatories.
- Emirates ID and residence visa copies, where applicable.
- Share certificates or an ownership register.
- Ultimate beneficial ownership information.
- A board resolution or signatory mandate.
- Proof of the company’s address.
- A company profile or business plan.
- Bank statements, contracts, or invoices, if requested.
- Tax registration documents, where applicable.


The[Federal Tax Authority’s Corporate Tax registration requirements](https://tax.gov.ae/en/services/corporate.tax.registration.aspx) also use documents such as the trade license, incorporation documents, identification for owners holding more than 25%, and proof of signatory authorization.


Requirements vary by company structure and business activity. Names, addresses, ownership percentages, and licensed activities should agree across every document.


## How to open a business bank account for your UAE company


### 1. Decide what the account needs to handle


Consider whether your company needs:


- Local and international transfers.
- AED and foreign-currency accounts.
- Employee cards.
- Cash or cheque deposits.
- Payroll and WPS support.
- Separate user permissions.
- Payment approval rules.
- Accounting integrations.


This gives you something more useful to compare than app screenshots.


### 2. Review the full cost


Read the provider’s Key Facts Statement and fee schedule. Check the minimum balance, monthly charges, transfer fees, foreign exchange rates, card costs, and account closure fees.


The cheapest plan can become rather expensive when every international supplier payment carries another charge.


### 3. Prepare a clear company profile


Explain what the business sells, who its customers and suppliers are, where they operate, and how much money the account is expected to receive and send.


Use specific wording. “General trading” may appear on the license, but the provider still needs to know what the company trades.


### 4. Submit the application


Many providers accept online applications. A video call, branch visit, or in-person identity check may still be required.


Shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories should be available if further verification is needed.


### 5. Complete the compliance review


The provider may request evidence supporting your source of funds and expected activity. Contracts, invoices, and bank statements can help answer these questions.


CBUAE’s three-business-day benchmark applies when the required standard due diligence documents are complete and satisfactory. More complex ownership structures or activities may require additional checks.


### 6. Assign account permissions


Once approved, confirm the company IBAN and decide who can prepare payments, approve them, issue cards, and reconcile transactions.


Giving everyone the admin password is quick. Working out who approved a payment three months later takes longer.

## Conclusion


Opening a UAE business bank account starts with a valid company licence, clear ownership records and a clear explanation of how the account will be used.


Prepare your documents early and look beyond account fees. Consider the full cost of payments, cards, foreign exchange and accounting as your business grows.


And as banking becomes more digital,[AI-native business banking](https://www.alaan.com/business-banking) can help you move beyond simply holding money to managing how it moves, gets spent, and gets recorded.


## FAQs


### How long does account opening take?


A complete application may meet CBUAE’s three-business-day benchmark. Additional compliance checks can extend the process.


### Can a free-zone company open an account?


Yes. Free-zone companies can apply using their license and incorporation documents, subject to the provider’s review.


### Can a non-resident apply?


Yes, although some providers may request additional proof of identity, address, tax residency, and source of funds.


### Is a minimum balance required?


It depends on the account. Some providers offer zero-balance plans, while others require a monthly average balance or charge a fee.
